title: Implement Experiment Logging for Signal Processing Metrics
description: The PulseScope Lite project currently processes video to extract a heart rate (BPM) but lacks a systematic way to track and evaluate the performance of its signal processing pipeline. This task involves implementing a basic experiment logging feature. The goal is to save key metrics—specifically the calculated BPM and the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the processed signal—to a user-specified CSV file. This will require modifications across the configuration, signal processing, and application entry point, as well as documentation updates.

project_spec.name: PulseScope Lite – Vital-Sign Camera Monitor
project_spec.description:
PulseScope Lite is a lightweight, C-based computer-vision application that continuously analyzes live webcam footage to estimate patients’ heart and respiratory rates by tracking subtle skin-tone fluctuations and thoracic motion. Designed for small outpatient clinics and home-care settings, the project implements an MVVM architecture to clearly separate low-level frame acquisition (Model), signal-processing/computer-vision logic (ViewModel), and the nurse-oriented UI dashboard (View).  

Despite its compact scope, PulseScope Lite integrates core MLOps concepts: a Factory Pattern loads different preprocessing and model variants at runtime; a simple experiment-tracking module logs model versions and hyperparameter selections to a local SQLite feature store; and an automated retraining pipeline can be scheduled nightly to fine-tune the lightweight CNN on freshly captured, clinician-labeled data. This focus on vital-sign extraction keeps the project emphatically healthcare-centric while remaining approachable for beginners.
dependencies: OpenCV C API (image capture & basic CV ops)
GLib/GObject (signals, event loop for MVVM bindings)
libmlpack (C bindings for lightweight CNN training)
